notes: Web 429 — NAV-LINK-NAVIGATION (Nov 12, 2026; layers on web 428). The owner's word, from a screen recording of the Dispatch card: 'Tapping the link does not navigate to anywhere. But that is supposed to be a secondary option — that is not supposed to be the primary option. [I] should be able to navigate in the navigation module with the link somewhere.' PROVEN STATE (code): the Navigator's Destination card offered search, the sent-pin paste bar and saved places, but nothing from the day's own dispatch; and the Maps links inside the dispatch Notes rendered through esc() as inert text — a tap did nothing. THE FIX, both doors, his order: PRIMARY (modules/navigator.js) — the Destination card now offers the ACTIVE dispatch's destinations under 'Today's dispatch': Go Empty and Hauling To, BY NAME, one tap routes to the pin. The pure read (navDispatchDestinations) takes the pin from the record's own site fields first (lat/lng, dumpLat/dumpLng — the v415 fields), then from the notes' labelled pins through the ONE link brain (PinLinks.extractPins); a destination whose notes carry a link but no readable pin keeps the link and the tap resolves it through PinLinks.resolveUrl before landing. The landing is the sent-pin landing (setDest auto-routes) with the visit recorded under the destination's own name (the Manifest law). No active dispatch (or a completed/cancelled one) → no block; the card is byte-identical. The paste-a-link door already stood in this card and is untouched. SECONDARY (modules/dispatch.js) — notes now render through dspNotesHtml on the active card, the completed face and the list rows: the same escaped text, each Maps link replaced in place by a small 'Maps pin' button. Its tap (dspNavigateNoteLink) offers navigation to the pin read from (1) the labelled pair the owning record's own notes set beside that link (dspNotesSitePins — the Nov 12 shape answers on-device, no network), (2) a pin inside the link itself (PinLinks.coordsFromUrl), (3) the link followed through PinLinks.resolveUrl; the landing is the card's own dspNavigatePin hand-off, and an unreadable link gets plain words, never an invented pin. SCOPE: link-based navigation entry points only — wording, routing, counting and every other screen untouched. Bench: the new suite tools/nav-link-navigation-v429-test.js — on 428 bytes it fails exactly the missing feature (1 passed / 18 failed); on 429 it passes in full, including behavioural runs of the real extractors against the EXACT Nov 12 notes text ('Go Empty To: (51.125222, -113.9828056) https://maps.app.goo.gl/31tR5SGgMHcsBLGHA Hauling To: (51.1225089, -114.0122197) https://maps.app.goo.gl/8FsunB9m3Rijgymq8'): both destinations offered by name with the pairs beside their labels, stored fields outranking notes, link-only destinations deferred to tap-time resolution, both notes links painted as buttons carrying their own URLs, a tap on either navigating to its labelled pair with no network, a declined offer navigating nowhere, and an unreadable link ending in plain words. Regression A/B vs the 428 baseline is reported in the ship record. VERDICT OWED IN HIS HANDS: on a real drive, the Navigator's Destination card offers today's Go Empty / Hauling To and one tap routes; and a tap on a Notes link offers its pin — not claimed until he taps it himself.
